messages:
bob_customer: Hey team, embedding calls started failing after we upgraded our JS client. Getting 400 'invalid input shape' for what used to be a working batch. Repro below, can someone take a look?

bob_customer: Repro curl (simplified):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/gzip' \ 
  --data-binary @payload.gz
```

bob_customer: payload.gz contains NDJSON lines that look like:

```
{"id":"1","vector": [0.12,0.23, ... 1535 values ...]}
{"id":"2","vector": [0.11,0.21, ... ]}
```

bob_customer: Previously we sent a plain JSON array of arrays: [[...],[...]] and it worked. After the client update it started wrapping each vector as an object with key `vector` and then gzipping as NDJSON to save memory. Now 100% of calls return 400 or sometimes 401 if token was near expiry.

alice_support: Thanks for the repro, bob. Two quick questions: 1) Which SDK/client version did you upgrade to? 2) Can you paste the exact error body we return (if any)? Logs/snips are fine.

bob_customer: Using our internal fork of `fast-vec@2.4.0` that changed the batch serializer. Error body from API is short:

```
{"error":"invalid input shape: expected top-level array of vectors or 'input' field; got object-per-line"}
```

bob_customer: We also intermittently see 401 with: `{"error":"invalid auth token"}` when the token is ~30s from expiry and large gz uploads take longer.

carla_eng: Quick triage notes: Redwood embeddings endpoint expects either a JSON array of vectors (application/json) or newline-delimited bare vectors (application/x-ndjson) where each line is the vector itself (e.g. `[0.1,0.2,...]`). It does not accept NDJSON objects like {"vector": [...]} unless you use our compatibility wrapper which your org is not using.

carla_eng: Also we validate vector length. If you send an object wrapper the server will attempt to coerce but may end up reading a different shape. Can you confirm the actual numeric count we're seeing? The logs show one request with mismatch: expected 1536 got 1535.

embed-bot: [ingest-check] trace 2523456789: validation failed -> dimension_mismatch (expected=1536, received=1535) at shard-3

bob_customer: Ah interesting — the client's serializer was doing `JSON.stringify(vec)` but there was a bug where the last element get dropped when converting Float32Array to Array for very large batches. So both shape (object vs array) AND dimension mismatch are happening.

alice_support: That lines up. Two actionable fixes:
  - Make the client emit raw vectors (array of numbers) when using JSON array payloads OR emit bare arrays per line for NDJSON (no wrapper object). Content-Type must match: `application/json` for array payloads, `application/x-ndjson` for ndjson. If gzipping, use `Content-Encoding: gzip` and keep Content-Type the same.
  - Add preflight validation in the client to assert each vector length == 1536 before send; return a clear error locally.

alice_support: Example good payloads:

JSON array (application/json):
```
[
  [0.12, 0.23, ... 1536 values ...],
  [0.11, 0.21, ... 1536 values ...]
]
```

NDJSON (application/x-ndjson with optional Content-Encoding: gzip):
```
[0.12,0.23,...]
[0.11,0.21,...]
```

alice_support: Example headers for gzipped NDJSON:
```
Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
Content-Encoding: gzip
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

dan_devex: Small note on auth: if uploads are large and token close to expiry, you can either extend token lifetime for upload flows or implement chunked uploads with short-lived signed URLs. Also add a retry for 401 that refreshes token instead of failing the whole batch.

bob_customer: Thanks — we patched the serializer to emit arrays, fixed the Float32->Array bug (off-by-one), and switched to `Content-Encoding: gzip` with `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`. We also added a client-side shape check before send and a token refresh-on-401 retry. Re-testing now.

bob_customer: Re-test results: 200 for large batches, no more 400. Also didn't see the 401 after adding token refresh. Upload times unchanged.

alice_support: Awesome — can you paste the minimal before/after diff? We'll include it in our KB for similar customer reports.

bob_customer: Diff (pseudo):
```
- const line = JSON.stringify({ id, vector: Array.from(vec) })
+ const line = JSON.stringify(Array.from(vec))
```
+ ensure headers: `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`, `Content-Encoding: gzip`
+ add `if (vec.length !== 1536) throw new Error('bad-dim')`
```

carla_eng: Thanks — we'll add a small note to the embedding input validation docs: "avoid object-wrapped vectors in NDJSON flows" and an example for gzipped NDJSON and token expiry patterns.

alice_support: Marking this thread resolved. If you hit anything else, reopen. :white_check_mark:
